_comment: CROSS-LANGUAGE PARITY FIXTURE for the Scryfall card object.
The same card JSON is built twice: card_engine/src/card_object.rs serves the engine path and
api/scryfall_compat/objects.py serves the SQL path. Both answer /cards/*, so a difference
between them is a difference a client can see, and nothing else compares them.
Each case is an engine row plus the object BOTH implementations produce from it, built with
base_url 'https://api.example/v1' unless the case names its own. card_object.rs asserts it in
Rust and test_scryfall_compat_objects.py asserts it in Python, so either one drifting turns its
own CI job red.
BYTES, key ORDER included: each side compares its compact output (no whitespace, UTF-8 unescaped)
with `expected` exactly as this file spells it, at every level -- the top level, every face,
every related card, `legalities`. Keep `expected` in wire order when editing it.
The cases carrying a `scryfall` block are API.SCRYFALL.COM'S OWN OBJECTS, fetched 2026-09-26
from the `uri` given, so the order they pin is Scryfall's rather than either writer's. Each
`row` is what the store holds for that printing; each `expected` is Scryfall's body with the
affiliate wrapper on the tcgplayer links unwrapped (both writers link the destinations
directly) and the keys in `removed` deleted -- keys this branch's store does not hold yet
(artist_ids, a face's artist_id, resource_id, preview, variation_of, content_warning, the
printed_* triple), which is all that stands between these objects and Scryfall's bytes.
To add a case: add the row, run both suites, and paste the object they agree on. If they do
not agree, that is the bug this file exists to find.

no marketplace ids means a name search per key
